claim: The failure of not all in the same existential frame is used to test an implicature of some.
evidence_summary: There were some children in the park is natural with no larger set salient. The stronger alternative can also be negated outside that frame.
finding: Syntactic substitutability is a weak test of an implicature. The distinction between proportional and non-proportional uses survives.
inference: Must a stronger scalar alternative fit the identical syntactic frame to contribute an implicature?

evidence.passage: §5.2, p. 364. The failure of not all in the same existential frame is used to test an implicature of some.
evidence.example: There were some children in the park can introduce an entirely new group. Where a particular class is salient, a speaker can add The rest of the class stayed at school. The stronger alternative need not occupy the postverbal NP slot.
evidence.establishes: Infelicity of not all in one existential frame gives no direct verdict on an inference about the salient class. The contrast between proportional and non-proportional uses remains.
